title: Minimax Transported Effect Estimation with Unknown Rough Densities and Polynomial Overlap Depletion
banked_reason: D0.5.G assessed subfield novelty, paper-score ceiling 7.2 below field threshold 7.4, not salvageable within this topic scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered frontier is confined to scalar polynomial boundary depletion with public powers and public response smoothness; it does not characterize general weak-overlap transport or unknown-geometry adaptation.

The implementation establishes termination under supplied representation contracts, but supplies neither a runtime guarantee nor evidence that its conservative public gates and constants yield useful finite-sample precision.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
Panel findings left unrepaired (the tier, not these, is the reason for the halt): related_work_inadequate@thm:finite-graded-jet-frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery pivoted from a single-trial graded jet claim that overlapped a banked predecessor to a two-trial pooled frontier. The final note derives matching finite-sample risk and honest interval length, a finite represented-input certificate, a strict pooling allocation wedge, and a scoped adaptation elbow; source statements for four cited probability/testing lemmas were attested. D0.5 judged the result sound but subfield because its scalar public-geometry scope cannot clear the fixed field novelty floor; Lean formalization did not begin.
tldr: The causal finite-sample frontier is \(\mathfrak R_{\mathbf n,m}\asymp\mathfrak L_{\mathbf n,m}\asymp m^{-1/2}+\Omega_{\mathbf n}(\mathbf a,s)\), attained by one finite graded jet estimator and a computable bias-aware connected interval for every independent sample-size ratio. Source and target density factors are unknown bounded measurable functions; response smoothness is public with \(s>1/2\). A finite public scale list, Gram/count gates, global sparse-cell fallback, and outward residual and rounding certificates give a terminating represented-input implementation with the same expected rate. No density smoothness index or density-radius compatibility is needed for this frontier. For \(0\le a_1<1<a_2\), \(n_1=\lceil N^\gamma\rceil\), and \(n_2=m=N\), the allocation transition is \(\gamma_*=(2s+a_1+1)/(2s+a_2+1)\). The source order is \(N^{-(s+1)/(2s+a_2+1)}\) below and at the transition, and \(N^{-\rho(\gamma)}\) above it, where \(\rho(\gamma)=\{\gamma(a_2-1)+(1-a_1)\}/\{2(a_2-a_1)\}\). The \((a_1,a_2,s,\gamma)=(0,2,1,4/5)\) example gives \(N^{-9/20}\) rather than \(N^{-2/5}\) for either source alone. The existing known-geometry plateau and honest-interval elbow results retain their stated scopes. The scalar check gives \(n^{-1/2}\), \(\sqrt{\log(en)/n}\), or \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) according as \(a<1\), \(a=1\), or \(a>1\); for \(s=a=2\) this is \(n^{-3/7}\). Unknown depletion geometry and restricted nonnested adaptation unions remain the separate open question.
gap: Published multi-trial transport papers identify the target effect and derive regular efficiency theory, but they do not characterize minimax risk or honest expected length when every source has its own vanishing boundary density. Single-source weak-overlap frontiers cannot encode a sample-size-dependent crossover among powers.
fill: The project makes the pooled Hölder information modulus the common frontier for all-estimator absolute error and fixed-class honest connected-interval length, supplies an observable optimal-recovery construction, proves a strict-pooling regime, and certifies that no fixed effective exponent reproduces it.
